appraisal_events.evidence: "Nous allons combiner ça, mais il ne faut pas que Swann le sache. Vous savez, il met un peu de froid."
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin plans a private lunch between Odette and Forcheville to be kept secret from Swann, explicitly because his presence dampens the mood, comparatively favoring newcomer Forcheville while pushing Swann to the margins of the clan's plans.

appraisal_events.evidence: "cria-t-elle au petit pianiste, afin de faire montre, devant un nouveau de l'importance de Forcheville, à la fois de son esprit et de son pouvoir tyrannique sur les fidèles."
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly exposes Mme Verdurin's sharp outburst at the pianist as a calculated performance staged to impress the newcomer Forcheville, undercutting her authority by revealing it as petty and self-serving.

status_effects.explanation: Swann is deliberately kept in the dark about a lunch between Odette and Forcheville because he is judged to 'put a damper' on things, marking his exclusion from an inner arrangement of the clan.
Forcheville is drawn into the clan's confidence and favored with a private arrangement involving Odette, precisely the access being denied to Swann.
The narrator's exposure of her performative tyranny over the pianist, staged to impress Forcheville, casts her local authority as insecure and self-serving rather than earning it neutrally.

ambiguities: Forcheville's flattering praise of Cottard ('il a de l'esprit comme quatre') is undercut by Mme Cottard's closing remark that he had in fact been speaking ill of Cottard; this hints at Forcheville's duplicity but the passage offers no explicit narrator judgment on it, so it was not elevated to a separate appraisal event.
